roles.title: Design Systems Engineer
roles.description: Build and maintain component libraries, tokens, and design-to-code workflows.
roles.flavor: Consistency at scale is an engineering problem.

roles.title: Frontend Developer
roles.description: Build performant, accessible web applications with modern frameworks.
roles.flavor: Code that works everywhere is code that ships.

roles.title: Junior Web Designer
roles.description: Create responsive, accessible web interfaces and design systems.
roles.flavor: Good design is obvious. Great design is invisible.

roles.title: UX Designer
roles.description: Research user needs, design flows, wireframes, and validate through testing.
roles.flavor: Design for the user, not the stakeholder.

cards.name: Attend Design Critique
cards.description: Sit in on a design review, usability test, or design system office hours.
cards.flavor: Watch how feedback shapes the product.

cards.name: Complete Partner Web Project
cards.description: Deliver the agreed web project: accessible components, documented APIs, and deployment guide.

cards.name: Build a Production Feature
cards.description: Design and implement a UI feature: component, page, or flow. Follow the design system.
cards.flavor: Design in Figma. Ship in code.

cards.name: Deliver Web Project
cards.description: Design and build the project: responsive pages, components, CMS integration, and QA.
cards.flavor: Responsive by default. Accessible by design.

cards.name: Deliver Design System Foundation
cards.description: Create tokens, core components, and documentation site for the partner's design system.

cards.name: Improve Accessibility
cards.description: Audit and fix WCAG violations: color contrast, keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, focus management.

cards.name: Build a Reusable Component
cards.description: Create a fully tested, documented, accessible component with variants and states.
cards.flavor: A component library is a product, not a project.

cards.name: Build a Volunteer Website
cards.description: Design and build a responsive site: IA, wireframes, UI, and frontend implementation.

cards.name: Measure UX Impact
cards.description: Explain how your work improved usability, accessibility, performance, or conversion.
cards.flavor: Good UX shows in the numbers.

cards.name: Design System Live
cards.description: Partner's products ship using the new design system. Measure consistency and velocity gains.

cards.name: Partner Site Improved
cards.description: Your work improved the partner's site: performance, accessibility, conversion, or developer velocity.

cards.name: Component Adopted
cards.description: Your component is used across multiple pages/products. Document adoption metrics.

cards.name: Feature Live in Production
cards.description: Your feature is live. Document the user-facing result and any metrics (conversion, engagement).
cards.flavor: Live is the only environment that matters.

cards.name: Document Web Project Learnings
cards.description: Write a case study: problem, user research, design iterations, tech choices, and results.

cards.name: Log Web Design Hours & Reflection
cards.description: Record hours and reflect on components built, design decisions, and cross-browser testing.
cards.flavor: Every component teaches a new constraint.

cards.name: Design System Handoff
cards.description: Walk partner team through the system: tokens, components, contribution model, and governance.
cards.flavor: A system without governance is just a library.

cards.name: Component Documentation
cards.description: Write component docs: API, usage examples, accessibility notes, and migration guide.

cards.name: Feature Reflection
cards.description: Write a reflection on the feature: user feedback, accessibility audit, and performance metrics.

cards.name: Showcase Partner Web Work
cards.description: Present your partner project: requirements, design process, technical implementation, and outcomes.
cards.flavor: Show the system, not just the screens.

cards.name: Volunteer Project Feedback
cards.description: Collect feedback from the nonprofit on usability, maintenance, and goal achievement.
cards.flavor: Client feedback is the ultimate test.

cards.name: Book Design Team Visit
cards.description: Arrange a visit to a product design team. Confirm date, NDA, and design critique invitation.
cards.flavor: See how design decisions happen at scale.

cards.name: Find Nonprofit Web Project
cards.description: Join a volunteer project building a website for a nonprofit or community group.
cards.flavor: Real users. Real constraints. Real impact.

cards.name: Design System Audit
cards.description: Audit partner's existing UI: inventory components, find inconsistencies, and prioritize standardization.
cards.flavor: Audit before you build. Measure before you cut.

cards.name: Partner Web Requirements
cards.description: Agree on deliverables with an industry partner: design system audit, component library, or migration.

cards.name: Set Up Design Token Pipeline
cards.description: Configure Style Dictionary or similar: tokens, build scripts, and platform outputs (iOS, Android, Web).
cards.flavor: Tokens are the single source of truth.

cards.name: Confirm Placement Details
cards.description: Agree tasks, dates, and hours with the design/dev team; confirm your mentor and repo access.

cards.name: Complete Web Design Onboarding
cards.description: Set up Figma, Storybook, and the component library. Review the design system documentation.
cards.flavor: Know the system before you extend it.

cards.name: Understand the Web Brief
cards.description: Clarify the brief: target audience, key journeys, tech stack, accessibility requirements, deadline.

cards.name: Research Industry Standards
cards.description: Study current best practices, pipelines, and quality bars for your discipline.
cards.flavor: Know the bar before you raise it.

cards.name: Create Personal Learning Plan
cards.description: Map skills to acquire, resources to use, and milestones to hit during the experience.
cards.flavor: A plan turns hope into progress.

cards.name: Set Up Portfolio Tracking
cards.description: Create a system to capture work-in-progress, feedback, and final pieces for your portfolio.
cards.flavor: Document as you go, not after.

cards.name: Establish Communication Routines
cards.description: Agree on check-in frequency, update formats, and escalation paths with your supervisor.
cards.flavor: Communication is a skill, not an afterthought.

cards.name: Define Success Metrics
cards.description: Agree on what "done well" looks like: quality, speed, innovation, or player impact.
cards.flavor: You can't hit a target you can't see.

cards.name: Prepare Questions for Mentor
cards.description: List specific technical, creative, and career questions to maximize mentor sessions.

cards.name: Prototype a Core System
cards.description: Build a quick proof-of-concept for a key mechanic, tool, or pipeline.

cards.name: Collaborate Cross-Discipline
cards.description: Work with a different discipline (art/code/design) to integrate a feature end-to-end.
cards.flavor: Great games are built at discipline boundaries.

cards.name: Optimize a Workflow
cards.description: Identify a bottleneck and implement a faster process, script, or template.

cards.name: Run a Playtest Session
cards.description: Observe players, take notes, and identify friction points in the experience.

cards.name: Create Technical Documentation
cards.description: Write clear docs for a system, API, or pipeline so others can use and maintain it.
cards.flavor: Documentation is empathy for your future self.

cards.name: Refactor for Maintainability
cards.description: Clean up messy code, rigs, or files to improve readability and reduce future bugs.

cards.name: Record Peer Feedback
cards.description: Document specific feedback from teammates and how you acted on it.

cards.name: Capture Before/After Comparison
cards.description: Show side-by-side evidence of improvement: performance, quality, or player experience.

cards.name: Write a Case Study Outline
cards.description: Structure a portfolio case study: problem, process, solution, result, reflection.

cards.name: Collect Quantitative Metrics
cards.description: Gather data: frame rates, load times, player retention, iteration speed, bug counts.

cards.name: Document a Failure & Recovery
cards.description: Record what went wrong, root cause analysis, and the fix that prevented recurrence.

cards.name: Create a Showcase Video/GIF
cards.description: Record a 30-second clip of your work in context: in-engine, in-game, or in-pipeline.

cards.name: Feature Adopted by Team
cards.description: Your prototype, tool, or process was adopted as standard practice by the team.

cards.name: Mentored a Peer
cards.description: Helped another student/junior improve their skills through guidance and knowledge sharing.

cards.name: Contributed to Shipped Content
cards.description: Your work is part of content that reached players, even in a small way.
cards.flavor: Shipped is the only metric that counts.

cards.name: Wild Card: Industry Veteran Insight
cards.description: A veteran shares hard-won wisdom. Use in place of any Setup, Action, or Proof card for any set.

cards.name: Wild Card: Cross-Discipline Workshop
cards.description: An intensive workshop bridges disciplines. Use in place of any card for any set.

cards.name: Wild Card: Personal Project Sprint
cards.description: A focused personal project fills a gap. Use in place of any card for any set.

sets.name: Block Placement
sets.why: A placement gives practical experience and, if it goes well, an employer reference.

sets.name: Employer Visit
sets.why: A visit builds industry understanding and useful contacts.

sets.name: Volunteering
sets.why: Volunteering shows reliability, initiative and teamwork.

sets.name: Live Project Brief
sets.why: A finished brief creates a portfolio piece that shows you can respond to a client's needs.

sets.name: Industry Partnership
sets.why: A partnership gives you specialist feedback and experience working with professionals.
